source.title: Should We Learn Most Likely Functions or Parameters?
source.authors: Shi-Kai Qiu; Tim G. J. Rudner; Sanyam Kapoor; Andrew Gordon Wilson

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares a new function-space regularizer with standard parameter-space MAP and reports held-out performance, but does not test any listed version's specific intervention or measurement.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study's own held-out performance comparisons. The authors' statements about prior work linking flat minima to generalization are cited background, not results from this study. Flatness measurements are not rows because this study does not measure whether they track the training–test gap.
record.test_reason: The study compares parameter-space MAP, function-space MAP and Laplacian regularization. None of its interventions or measurements tests V1–V8. Its flatness experiments measure Hessian curvature or loss along filter-normalized directions, without testing magnitude-aware sharpness as a predictor or ranking of generalization gaps. The listed findings motivate discussion rather than serve as an established tool whose performance is evaluated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that function-space MAP offers potential generalization, robustness and calibration benefits, especially with a well-motivated prior, but also has pathological optima and substantial computational costs. Its scalable Laplacian approximation generally yields comparable or slightly better image-classification accuracy and often better calibration; function-space MAP need not better approximate the Bayesian model average.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces function-space MAP and its Laplacian approximation as a regularizer and compares them with parameter-space MAP; does not reproduce the original studies' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: In synthetic regression, test RMSE depends on the evaluation distribution and the assumed observation-noise scale. Image-classification results also vary by dataset and evaluation-point distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: FS-MAP lowers synthetic test RMSE and reduces fitting of observation noise when the model is well specified; its performance depends on the evaluation distribution and assumed noise scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Function-space MAP can improve synthetic regression generalization under suitable modeling assumptions, but can underfit under misspecification.

fits_no_version.finding: L-MAP has lower mean test RMSE on seven of eight UCI datasets and broadly comparable image-classification accuracy, including transfer learning and CIFAR-10.1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Laplacian regularization provides dataset-dependent improvements in regression and generally comparable image-classification accuracy relative to parameter-space MAP.

fits_no_version.finding: L-MAP is described as slightly more robust to training-label noise on CIFAR-10.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Laplacian regularization can modestly improve held-out accuracy under training-label corruption.

fits_no_version.finding: FS-MAP reduces average Hessian curvature in synthetic regression; L-MAP produces flatter filter-normalized loss profiles for image classifiers. These results do not measure the gap-ranking relationship in V7.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Function-space MAP and its Laplacian approximation can favor flatter solutions under the study's curvature and loss-profile measurements.

record.problems: The synthetic generalization plots report means and standard deviations over three seeds but provide no tabulated values in the supplied text. Neural-network accuracy differences are often small; the paper notes that the prior may not represent the data-generating process well. Figure-only label-noise results have no numerical values stated.
record.rows_left_out: Rows for calibration, selective prediction, negative log-likelihood, and loss-landscape curvature were omitted because they do not directly measure the training–test generalization gap or a listed version's named property. The paper's cited claims about flat minima and generalization are not its own experimental results.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning budgets and recovery through broader tuning or optimizer changes.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, excessive dropout and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance tracking training–test gaps among similarly fitted networks, including ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All rows remain unlinked to V1–V8. Their states are cannot_determine relative to those versions, rather than verdicts on whether the proposed regularizer works. No claim-version verdicts or version-relevant missing rows are warranted.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting fixed random labels with generalization on natural labels.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD for generalization; optimizer choice is not the tested intervention.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare its ranking of generalization gaps against norm- or margin-based measures.
